title: minimize presubmit startup and introduce release peacekeeper
author: Ava Martinez
release_notes: Reduce presubmit cold-start latency; Merge-prober prevents transient green merges; Consolidated presubmit pools reduce flakiness; Updated several GitHub Actions to pinned SHAs; Small dependency bumps and lockfile refresh.
description: Context and goal: presubmit job start-up time and noisy short-lived runners have been a major source of feedback delay and flakiness for teams. This PR reduces cold-start latency for the majority of PRs by consolidating presubmit runner pools, standardizing a slim preflight image, and introducing a merge-prober (Release Peacekeeper) that gates merges briefly to catch transient CI flakiness and release automation race conditions. Summary of changes: 1) Add a lightweight presubmit bootstrap image (ci/images/presubmit-slim.Dockerfile) optimized for common language toolchains and with layered caching for pip/go/npm installs; 2) Rework .github/workflows/presubmit.yml to introduce fast/slow lanes and to run a trimmed lint/smoke set in the fast lane; 3) Consolidate presubmit worker pool definitions to ci/runner/pools.yaml and add pool affinity rules to reduce runner churn; 4) Add a merge-prober service (ci/tools/merge_prober/) that watches merge events and re-triggers a short sanity check across a matrix before the final merge commit; 5) Pin several GitHub Action SHAs and bump action-tooling in .github/actions/ to reduce unexpected upgrades; 6) Refresh lockfiles (package-lock.json, go.sum) and update small transitive deps flagged by dep-audit. Why this is safe: the slim presubmit image runs only a curated set of checks by default; full integration tests remain on the slow lane. The merge-prober intentionally runs a short set of smoke checks and will not block manual merges with an override label if an urgent hotfix is required. Related: ENG-9876 (presubmit perf), ENG-1023 (release hardening), SUP-412 (customer incident that motivated faster feedback). Checklist: - [x] CI green on fast/slow lanes - [x] pool size validated in staging - [x] no regressions in lint output - [x] docs updated (docs/dev/ci-presubmit.md) - [x] rollback plan documented (ci/rollback/README.md). Commits: see commits array below. Files changed (high level): see files_changed array below. Review conversation (short): reviewers asked for clearer signal boundaries between fast and slow lanes and for an opt-out for large repos; implemented by adding explicit path filters and a repository-level opt-out label. Priya requested that the merge-prober retry logic back off exponentially; updated accordingly. Liam validated the pinned action SHAs and ran a canary across 10 repos. CI results: initial lint flake due to a transitive eslint rule, fixed by a lockfile refresh; subsequent CI pass on main matrix. Merge notes: merged by squash after two approvals and a final canary run across staging. Post-merge actions: monitor presubmit latency metric (ci.presubmit.startup_ms) for 72 hours, watch requeue rate and merge-prober false-positive rate, and follow up with a staged rollout of pool consolidation if any service team reports regression.
